blocks.text: Amines that dissolve in water give weakly alkaline solutions, as ammonia does, because they react partly with water to form OH- ions: NH3 + H2O <=> NH4+ + OH- (pKb 4.75); CH3CH2NH2 + H2O <=> CH3CH2NH3+ + OH-; C6H5NH2 + H2O <=> C6H5NH3+ + OH- (pKb 9.38).

The basicity of an amine depends on how available the lone pair on nitrogen is. The larger Kb (or the smaller pKb), the stronger the base. Electron-donating alkyl groups on the nitrogen increase basicity, and electron-withdrawing groups decrease it. Basicity usually also indicates how strongly nucleophilic a compound is.

items: Ethanamine is a stronger base than ammonia (and slightly stronger than methanamine); alkylamines in general are stronger bases than ammonia.

Ammonia is a stronger base than aromatic amines such as phenylamine. In phenylamine the nitrogen atom is planar and its lone pair is in a p orbital that overlaps with the delocalised pi electrons of the benzene ring, so the lone pair is less available to accept a proton.

blocks.alt: A benzene ring in perspective between two green rings of delocalised pi electrons, one above and one below the ring. The ring is bonded to an N atom with two green p-orbital lobes, one up and one down, and two H atoms (one behind, one in front). Arrows point from the lobes to the ring clouds.

blocks.text: Because they are bases, ammonia and ethanamine react with acids to form salts: the nitrogen donates its lone pair to form a dative bond with a proton. NH3 + HCl -> NH4+ Cl-; CH3CH2NH2 + HCl -> CH3CH2NH3+ Cl- (ethylammonium chloride).

blocks.title: Did you know?
blocks.text: The foul smell of fish is due to trimethylamine, (CH3)3N (N,N-dimethylmethanamine). When lemon juice is sprinkled on fish its acid reacts with the amine to form a salt, so the smell is reduced; vinegar does the same.
